title: impact.json
description: Deterministic sf-impact-tests output: direct referrers and counts per seed, shared references, selected and disjoint possible tests with shortest witnesses, and change-relevant confidence. Parsed paths select to depth. First-hop member text requires owner evidence in the same file; LWC text never selects. No containment re-expansion. All integer fields require integer JSON tokens; floating tokens such as 1.0 or 1e0 are refused even when mathematically integral. Draft 2020-12 cannot express that lexical distinction; readers enforce it. Normative relations checked by the reader: confidence is full exactly when gaps is empty; unverified input provenance has the corresponding unverified_refs reason. Every evidence/reference ID names an entry in references; direct referrer tiers and distinct counts agree with those entries, and selected and possible tests are disjoint. These relations require comparisons between values and remain prose rather than structural schema keywords. Schema version 1 uses closed objects. Readers refuse unknown schema versions; any added field, including an optional field, requires a schema version bump.

depth.description: Maximum incoming hops used for selection and possible evidence, default 2. Zero still reports direct counts, convention and changed-test selection.

seeds.description: Sorted seed identities: every changed symbol and touched name, or all declarations matching CLI queries.

queries.description: Explicit --symbol resolutions, sorted. Matching is case-insensitive against qualified symbol, method without parameters, or unqualified declaration name.

items.description: Query resolution; ambiguity is visible rather than choosing a declaration.

tests.description: Selected @IsTest classes from changed, convention, parsed paths through depth, corroborated first-hop textual mentions, trigger DML and platform entries. Unpackaged tests are included by default. A textual member match needs its owner, an enclosing type or a dispatch type named in the same file (textual type-name evidence or a parsed reference into the type).

untested.description: Changed owning classes with no selected test, plus seed/reached triggers without selected DML tests. Test classes are omitted.

confidence.description: partial only for gaps that could involve the change: changed-file gaps, related unresolved or ambiguous parsed names, missing changed declarations, scope errors, reached Apex parse/skipped gaps, or uncovered trigger/dynamic bindings. Otherwise full.

gaps.description: Changed-file gaps and gaps involving seeds or symbols reached through parsed paths, with source file and line (null only when the input supplies none). Selected Apex parse gaps also count. Weak-only reachability does not create new relevant names; those diagnostics remain counted separately. Inputs that were not verified to go together are a reason too: see `unverified_refs` under gap.

unresolved.description: Reference IDs of unresolved names matching a seed or a symbol reached through parsed paths in a compatible namespace. Weak-only names and unrelated unresolved names in reached files remain diagnostic counts.

items.description: Integer reference ID. Resolve with references[ID as a string]; IDs are sorted input row indices and need not be contiguous.

collisions.description: The duplicate API identities in refs that this query reached: a group is here when the walk reached any of its declarations, the seeds included. The others are left out and counted in `diagnostics.unreached_collision`. Classes, interfaces and enums share a namespace.

symbol.description: Representative spelling, deterministic. Callable symbols preserve owner and member source spelling; parameter types are canonical: lowercase throughout, with System. removed from primitive and collection names, Iterable, Iterator, Object and SObject, and arrays written recursively as list<...>, without spaces. For example, Account.process(System.List<Id>) and Account.process(Id[]) both become Account.process(list<id>).

declarations.description: Every declaration of this name and type namespace.

errors.description: Unknown queries or changed symbols missing from refs. The CLI writes this document and exits 1. Invalid input or arguments instead fail on stderr. sf-impact-render refuses any document with errors, even when structurally valid.

reason.description: Unknown query or missing non-removed changed declaration.

line.description: Changed declaration line, or null if absent.

possible.description: Prominent weak-evidence list, never selected: uncorroborated first-hop member names, longer paths containing textual evidence, or any LWC-to-Apex textual path. Tests selected through another route or convention are omitted from this disjoint list.

items.description: Possible test with reasons and one shortest witness.

references.description: Shared original reference rows keyed by stable integer IDs written as JSON object keys. Contains direct referrers, witness/proof rows and relevant unresolved rows only; each row appears once regardless of seed count. Keys are canonical unsigned decimal u64 integers, without signs or leading zeroes (except 0 itself).

additionalProperties.description: Original input reference, without the JSONL row discriminator.

diagnostics.description: Counts by kind of input diagnostics unrelated to the change, including unrelated unresolved/ambiguous names and metadata already searched textually. These do not lower confidence.

unresolved.description: Number of diagnostic or reference rows.

ambiguous.description: Number of diagnostic or reference rows.

parse_error.description: Number of diagnostic or reference rows.

skipped_file.description: Number of diagnostic or reference rows.

unsupported_element.description: Number of diagnostic or reference rows.

unmodelled_file.description: Number of diagnostic or reference rows.

unreached_collision.description: Number of collision groups, not rows: the duplicate API identities in refs none of whose declarations this query reached, which `collisions` leaves out. Written only when it is not zero.

provenance.description: The writer and input provenance, verified again by sf-impact-render. Schema 1 is the first impact format with provenance; older documents are refused. Input envelopes must be valid and compatible by the same rules as sf-impact-tests. With changed input, every unverified refs input must have its confidence reason. This identifies inputs, not a cryptographic signature of report contents.

node.description: One declaration or evidence identity, including its location.

symbol.description: API symbol with overload parameters. For an undeclared source, its referrer name or file path. Callable symbols preserve owner and member source spelling; parameter types are canonical: lowercase throughout, with System. removed from primitive and collection names, Iterable, Iterator, Object and SObject, and arrays written recursively as list<...>, without spaces. For example, Account.process(System.List<Id>) and Account.process(Id[]) both become Account.process(list<id>).

type.description: Declaration kind; file for a source without a declaration, unknown for an untyped touched name.

package.description: Normalised scope directory. Together with type and symbol this is the API identity.

file.description: Declaration file at head, or evidence file for an undeclared or removed seed. Distinguishes colliding declarations.

line.description: First declaration line, or evidence line for an undeclared touched name. Null when the input supplies no line.

scope.description: Scope provenance from extraction. Null for a node that refs do not declare: a removed symbol, a touched name or a file. Never inferred from directory spelling.

reference.description: Original reference fields without the JSONL row discriminator; no tier or ambiguity is erased.

oneOf.description: A reference read from syntax. A reference is a row unless it is proven to be the Apex platform's alone: a platform name (`String`, `System.debug`), or a member of a value whose static type is proven to be a platform type. The proof is narrow: a platform class without type arguments returns platform types, and a collection returns its elements from the methods that are modelled. A platform type with type arguments, a collection method that is not modelled, or a call that produced no row proves nothing, and what follows is reported with `unknown_type`. A platform name in front of a name does not make it the platform's: `Schema.Invoice__c`, `Label.Greeting` and `Flow.Interview.Welcome` are rows. Collections and primitives written with their namespace (`System.List<Foo>`) are the same types as without. Not finding a declaration is never a reason to leave a reference out.

kind.description: `call`: a method call. `construct`: `new T(..)`, `this(..)` or `super(..)`. `type`: a type named in a declaration (a field, variable, parameter or return type, a type argument), in `instanceof`, as `T.class`, an object named in the describe form `SObjectType.Invoice__c`, or an object that metadata declares, named through a member of it (`Invoice__c.SObjectType`, `Settings__c.getInstance()`). `cast`: the type of a cast. `extends`, `implements`: a supertype. `static_access`: a member reached through a type name (`Type.member`), a static field or enum value used without its type inside the type that declares it or in a `switch` label, an object's field token (`Invoice__c.Total__c`, also written `Schema.Invoice__c.Total__c` or `SObjectType.Invoice__c.fields.Total__c`), or a custom label (`Label.Greeting`). `soql_object`, `soql_field`: an object or field named in an embedded SOQL or SOSL query; a field is prefixed with the object it is selected from and may be a relationship path (`Account.Owner.Name`, `Account.Contacts`). Where metadata declares the fields of a path, the path is one row for each field along it, all at the place of the path: `Carrier__r.Region__c` selected from `Shipment__c` is `Shipment__c.Carrier__c` and `Carrier__c.Region__c`, and a child relationship (`Parcels__r`) is the lookup field that makes it. `dml_object`: the object type of the operand of a DML statement or of `Database.insert(..)` and its siblings. `dml_field`: the external ID field of an `upsert`. `sobject_field`: a field set in a record initialiser, `new Account(Name = ..)`. `trigger_object`: the object a trigger is on.

oneOf.description: Flow object/field names, Apex action classes (or unresolved names for unmodelled action types), subflows, screen components, labels, custom permissions and custom metadata records; LWC Apex methods, schema names, labels, custom permissions, message channels, components, targets and objects. Apex imports retain every overload (ambiguous_overload), or all inherited candidates through divergent types (ambiguous_receiver). Object, field, label, custom permission, custom metadata type/record and message channel references resolve through the declarative catalog, with the same relationship traversal and collision rules as Apex. Labels use Label.X (namespace: Label.ns.X), channels MessageChannel.X__c. Resolved permissions use their declaration symbol X; undeclared permissions retain CustomPermission.X. Targets retain their literal lightning__ spelling as unresolved because no target declaration is modelled. Untyped dotted references yield unknown_type. Reference leaves and merge tokens are read in every Flow subtree; an unknown structure with an uninterpreted leaf is an `unsupported_element` row. Resolved custom metadata records use their declaration symbol Type.Record; undeclared records retain Type__mdt.Record. Their fields use Type__mdt.Field. Namespaced components use ns:camelName.

referenced.description: What is referred to. With `resolution` `declaration` this is the `symbol` of a declaration row of the kind `referenced_type` says, except with `detail` `ambiguous_overload`, where it is the method without parameters (`MathUtil.clamp`), and `ambiguous_receiver`, where it is the name as written (a bare member or type name). Where a name is declared more than once and the declarations differ in case, it is the spelling that sorts first. Otherwise it is the name as written at the reference, without a `Schema.` or `System.` qualifier in front of an object or a label.

referenced_type.description: What kind of thing `referenced` is. With `resolution` `declaration`, the `type` of the declaration it is, or of every candidate; `class` stands for any Apex type. Otherwise the kind of thing the syntax names, where it names one: a call names a `method`; a type name a `class`, as Apex has one namespace for types, which an SObject that no file declares shares; a query names an `object` and its fields `object_field`s; a Flow or a Lightning web component names each thing as what it is. Required with `resolution` `declaration`, except where candidates are of different kinds. Absent where the kind is not known, as for a static access through a name that nothing declares: the name may then be of any kind.

resolution.description: `declaration`: `referenced` is declared in scope, by Apex or, for an object, a field of one or a label, by metadata. `external`: it is in a namespace listed in the config file (`ns.Type`, `ns__Object__c`), or is a member of a type in one; expected, not a gap. `unresolved`: neither, and not proven to be the platform's; a gap in what this file can say. A standard object or field that no metadata file in the repository declares (`Account`, `Invoice__c.Name`) is `unresolved`, and so is a member of a type that is not declared in scope (`Account.get`, `Missing.run`).

detail.description: Present when the reference could not be pinned to exactly one declaration, and says why. `ambiguous_overload`: several overloads fit the call and the argument types do not decide; `candidates` lists them. `ambiguous_receiver`: the reference is reached through a name that is declared more than once with declarations that differ, or through an earlier reference that was itself ambiguous, or, for a field, through a lookup that is declared more than once to different objects, so it is one of several declarations; `candidates` lists every one it may be. This over-reports by design: nothing is hidden or preferred among them. It applies to calls, constructions, static accesses and type names alike. `unknown_type`: the type of the receiver of a call, of the operand of DML, or of the value a `switch` is on could not be established from the source; `referenced` is then the bare member name, or `SObject`. Reported whether or not anything declared has that name. `no_member`: the type is declared in scope but it and its supertypes declare no such member, or a bare name is declared nowhere in reach.

candidates.description: With `ambiguous_overload` or `ambiguous_receiver`: the symbols of the declarations the reference may be to, sorted, each once. Present with those two details and with no other.

referrer.description: The `symbol` of the innermost declaration that contains the reference: a method, constructor or field, else the type or trigger; in a metadata file, the component the file declares, or the label. Flow and LWC references use the Flow or bundle name, including auxiliary bundle files. Null where no declaration contains the reference.

package.description: The scope directory the file is under: a `packageDirectories` path or an `unpackagedMetadata` path from sfdx-project.json, relative to the root, with `/` separators whatever the project file uses.

file.description: Path of the file relative to the root, with `/` separators.

line.description: Line of the reference, counting from 1. For a call or a static access, the line of the member name.

column.description: Byte offset of the reference within its line, counting from 1. For a UTF-16 file, the offset in its UTF-8 transcoding.

oneOf.description: A whole-word, case-insensitive occurrence of a declared `name` in a file in scope, comments and string literals included: what a grep for the name would find. Independent of the parsed tier, so a reference found by both has a row in each. Names shorter than the configured minimum length (6 by default) are not looked for unless the config file's allow-list names them. A file is text if and only if it is valid UTF-8, or UTF-16 (LE or BE) with a BOM that decodes without error, and the decoded content contains no NUL (U+0000). A file that cannot be searched has a `skipped_file` row instead.

referenced.description: The word as written in the file. It equals the `name` of at least one declaration, ignoring case; it may be an occurrence of any of them or of none.

referrer.description: The `symbol` of the innermost declaration that contains the reference: a method, constructor or field, else the type or trigger; in a metadata file, the component the file declares, or the label. Flow and LWC references use the Flow or bundle name, including auxiliary bundle files. Null where no declaration contains the reference.

package.description: The scope directory the file is under: a `packageDirectories` path or an `unpackagedMetadata` path from sfdx-project.json, relative to the root, with `/` separators whatever the project file uses.

file.description: Path of the file relative to the root, with `/` separators.

line.description: Line of the reference, counting from 1. For a call or a static access, the line of the member name.

column.description: Byte offset of the reference within its line, counting from 1. For a UTF-16 file, the offset in its UTF-8 transcoding.

oneOf.description: A reference read from the structure of a metadata file: an object, field or validation rule, a permission set or profile, or a custom metadata record. Told apart from a reference read from Apex by its `kind`. As there, not finding a declaration is never a reason to leave a reference out, and neither is the thing being the platform's: a granted `standard-` tab is a row. The one exception is a constant of `$Api` or `$System` in a formula, which names nothing. An element of such a file that is not read for references has an `unsupported_element` row unless it is known to hold no name; a reference is never to an empty name.

kind.description: `lookup`: the object a lookup or master-detail field points at; for a metadata relationship field, `EntityDefinition`, `FieldDefinition` or a custom metadata type. `lookup_filter`: a field that a lookup filter compares: a field of the object looked up, written with it (`Carrier__c.Region__c`), a field of the object the lookup is on (`$Source.Weight__c`), or a field of a global, as in a formula. `controlling_field`: the field that controls this one: the controlling field of a dependent picklist, or the field of a custom metadata type that says which object a metadata relationship to a field is about. `display_field`: the field a validation rule shows its error on. `value_set`: the global value set a picklist takes its values from. `formula`: a name in a formula field, in a field's default value, or in the condition of a validation rule: a field, or what a global names (`$Label.Greeting`, `$Permission.Can_Approve`, `$Setup.Settings__c.Limit__c`, `$CustomMetadata.Plugin__mdt.Billing.Handler__c`, `$User.Region__c`, `$ObjectType.Invoice__c.Fields.Total__c`). A relationship path (`Account__r.Region__c`) is one row for each field along it, all at the start of the path: the lookup, then the field it reaches. Names in strings and comments are not references. `summary`: a field that a roll-up summary sums, filters on or joins on. `grant`: something a permission set or profile grants access to: a class, an object, a field, a Flow, a tab (a `standard-` tab too), a custom permission, a custom metadata type or a custom setting. `cmdt_field`: a field of its type that a custom metadata record sets, whatever it sets it to. `cmdt`: something a custom metadata record names in a value or in its own name. A value of a metadata relationship field names what the field's declared type says: an object (`EntityDefinition`), a field of the object that the controlling field's value names (`FieldDefinition`; as written and `unresolved` if the record does not say which object), or a record of another type; such a row is there whether or not anything declares the name. Any other value, and the record's own name, is a row only if it equals a declared symbol, ignoring case: a class, a Flow, an object and so on; a class bound by a framework and a value that matches by coincidence look the same here, so the row says which field it came from. `cmdt_type`: the custom metadata type a record is a record of.

referenced.description: What is referred to. With `resolution` `declaration` this is the `symbol` of a declaration row of the kind `referenced_type` says, except with `detail` `ambiguous_receiver`, where it is the field name as written. Otherwise it is the name as written; where a relationship path cannot be followed, the rest of the path as written, after the last object that was reached (`Account.Owner.Manager.Name`).

referenced_type.description: What kind of thing `referenced` is, as the source says: the `type` of the declaration it resolves to or would resolve to. `class` stands for any Apex type. `lwc` is a Lightning web component bundle, which a custom metadata value can equal the name of. `tab` and `global_value_set` are kinds of thing that metadata names and this tool does not yet declare. Absent only on a `formula` row, for a global that is not known (`$Action.Account.New`).

resolution.description: `declaration`: declared in scope. `external`: in a namespace listed in the config file (`ns__Object__c`, `ns__Class`); expected, not a gap. `unresolved`: neither: a standard object or field that no file in the repository declares, a Flow that is not in scope, a tab or a global value set, or a name that is wrong; a gap in what this file can say.

detail.description: `ambiguous_receiver`: the field is reached through a lookup that is declared more than once, to different objects, so it is one of several declarations; `candidates` lists every one it may be. Nothing is chosen among them.

candidates.description: With `ambiguous_receiver`: the symbols of the declared fields the reference may be to, sorted, each once. An object the path may also lead to that does not declare the field is not among them: it has an `unresolved` row of its own at the same place.

referrer.description: The `symbol` of the component the file declares.

source_field.description: On a `cmdt` row, and on no other: the field of the record whose value names `referenced`, or `DeveloperName` where it is the record's own name.

package.description: The scope directory the file is under: a `packageDirectories` path or an `unpackagedMetadata` path from sfdx-project.json, relative to the root, with `/` separators whatever the project file uses.

file.description: Path of the file relative to the root, with `/` separators.

line.description: Line of the name in the file, counting from 1. A reference that comes from the file's name (`cmdt_type`, and `cmdt` from `DeveloperName`) is at line 1, column 1.

column.description: Byte offset of the reference within its line, counting from 1. For a UTF-16 file, the offset in its UTF-8 transcoding.

hop.description: One reference hop in the shortest witness; reference rows are shared, never embedded here.

target.description: Target declaration, or trigger for a trigger_dml bridge.

reference.description: Integer reference ID. Resolve with references[ID as a string]; IDs are sorted input row indices and need not be contiguous.

via.description: Why this edge reaches the seed: reference, seeded member, same-signature dispatch, targeted owner binding, trigger DML, or platform_entry (parsed owning-type/constructor reference when a method seed has no parsed incoming edge after dispatch and bindings). Expansions add no extra hop beyond the reference and never re-expand reached members.

evidence.description: Reference IDs proving dispatch inheritance or the trigger-to-object binding; empty for ordinary links.

items.description: Integer reference ID. Resolve with references[ID as a string]; IDs are sorted input row indices and need not be contiguous.

ambiguous.description: The reference has several possible targets or sources, candidates or a resolution limitation.

hit.description: Direct source/tier group with unique reference IDs and the target expansions those references may reach.

references.description: Distinct original reference IDs of this tier. Each row is stored once at document level.

items.description: Integer reference ID. Resolve with references[ID as a string]; IDs are sorted input row indices and need not be contiguous.

ambiguous.description: At least one of these references is ambiguous.

routes.description: Distinct referenced targets/expansions in this group. The reference IDs themselves appear only once per source and tier, even when a class seeds many members.

group.description: Referrers grouped by the kind of their source declaration; the tiers stay separate.

type.description: Declaration kind; file for a source without a declaration, unknown for an untyped touched name.

textual.description: Whole-word sites, including declarations, comments and strings.

changed_symbol.description: A symbol that the difference adds, modifies or removes, on the evidence of one changed file. A symbol is a declaration: at head a `declaration` row of refs.jsonl, at base what the base version of the file declares, read with the same code from the text that delta.jsonl gives. A declaration at base and one at head are the same symbol if they have the same package, kind of thing and name, ignoring case, whatever the file is called at each. The two versions compared are those of one file: a file changed in place, a file that moved, or a file that was deleted and a file that was added which are the same thing in the same package directory, because they declare the same symbol at the top, or are the `-meta.xml` companion of an Apex file of the same name. Those two are read as one file that moved and changed, and their lines are compared by `sf-impact-changed`, as delta.jsonl compares the lines of a file changed in place. So a class that moved and was edited has only what was edited marked. Where it is not one deleted file and one added file that are the same thing, but more of either, none is chosen, and what they declare is removed and added, as is a declaration that goes from one changed file to another by any other way. A symbol has one row for each changed file that marks it: an LWC bundle of which two files changed has two. Declarations of one name in several files (`collision`) are not merged and none is chosen: each has the rows that the change to its own file gives it.

row.description: Input row discriminator, carried unchanged from changed.jsonl.

symbol.description: The API name, as the `symbol` of a refs.jsonl declaration: `Invoice`, `Invoice.total()`, `Invoice.round(decimal,integer)`, `Invoice__c.Total__c`, `Label.Greeting`, the name of a Flow or of an LWC bundle. A method or constructor includes its parameter types, so a change of signature is one symbol `removed` and another `added`. Callable symbols preserve owner and member source spelling; parameter types are canonical: lowercase throughout, with System. removed from primitive and collection names, Iterable, Iterator, Object and SObject, and arrays written recursively as list<...>, without spaces. For example, Account.process(System.List<Id>) and Account.process(Id[]) both become Account.process(list<id>).

type.description: What kind of thing the symbol is: the `type` of a refs.jsonl declaration.

package.description: The scope directory that `file` is under. Part of what a symbol is: a class moved from one package directory to another is `removed` from the one and `added` to the other.

file.description: The changed file that is the evidence for this row, relative to the root, with `/` separators. For `change` `removed` its path at base, otherwise its path at head. Usually the file that declares the symbol; with `reason` `whole_file` it can be another file of the same component: a file of an LWC bundle other than the one the bundle is declared in, or the `-meta.xml` companion of an Apex class or trigger.

change.description: `added`: declared at head and not at base. `modified`: declared at both, and the change marks it. `removed`: declared at base and not at head. An LWC bundle is at base, or at head, if any file of it is.

reason.description: Why the symbol is in this file. `hunk`: lines that the difference changes, adds or takes away are lines of the declaration, and of no smaller declaration inside it; `hunks` lists the hunks. A line marks the innermost declaration around it: a method, a constructor, a field, an inner class, or the class where the line is in no member; declarations on the same lines are marked together. A line that a declaration starts or ends on can hold more than that declaration: another member, the rest of a class header, the end of an initializer, which has no lines of its own to be found by. Such a line cannot say which of them changed, and marks every declaration around it, the type they are in too, unless it is a line of one declaration alone: only declarations on the very same lines start or end on it, and nothing but white space is before them on their first line or after them on their last. That is read from the source of each version of the file, for its own lines. A comment after a member counts as something else on the line. Each version of the file is read by its own lines: a line that the head has new or changed marks the declaration around it at head, and a line that the base had and the head has not marks the declaration it was in at base, if the head still declares that. So an annotation taken from above a method marks the method. A hunk that leaves no line at head also marks the innermost declaration at head around the gap it leaves: lines taken out of a method mark the method, and a member that is removed whole marks the class it was in. A line outside every declaration of its file, such as a comment above a class, marks what the file declares at the top. A blank line counts like any other, and so does a change of white space alone: nothing is ignored. In a metadata file that is one component, every line is inside the declaration. `whole_file`: the file as a whole marks the symbol and no line does: the file was added or deleted; or its content changed and there are no lines for it (`binary`); or it is a file of the component other than the one with the declaration's lines, where `hunks` still lists the lines that changed: a file of an LWC bundle, or the `-meta.xml` companion of an Apex file, which marks what the Apex file of its name declares at the top, whether the companion is changed, added, deleted or moved, and for one that goes from one Apex file's name to another's both what it left and what it joined; or the symbol is new by its name or package alone, as the unchanged method of a class that was given another name, or everything in a file that moved to another package directory. `removed`: the symbol is declared in the base version of a file that is still there at head, modified or moved, or that went on in an added file (see `symbol`), and the head version no longer declares it; this goes with `change` `removed`. So it is for a file that moved to a place where it is another kind of file or out of scope: an Apex file that becomes a file of a bundle no longer declares anything. A symbol removed with its whole file has `whole_file`.

start.description: First line of the declaration in `file`, counting from 1, annotations and modifiers included: at base for `change` `removed`, at head otherwise. Absent, with `end`, where the lines of the declaration are not in `file`.

end.description: Last line of the declaration in `file`, inclusive.

previous_file.description: Present on a `modified` row whose `file` was added while the file that declared the symbol at base was deleted: the path of that file. The base lines of `hunks` are lines of it.

hunks.description: The hunks that mark the symbol, in the order of the file. Present with `reason` `hunk`, and with `whole_file` for a file of a component whose own lines changed. Their head lines are lines of `file`; their base lines are lines of the same file at base, or of `previous_file` where the row has one.

collision.description: At head, another declaration has this name, ignoring case, and is the same kind of thing: the `collision` of the refs.jsonl declaration. For `change` `removed`: at head some declaration still has this name and is the same kind of thing, in another file or another package directory, so the name is gone from here and not from the repository. Classes, interfaces and enums share one namespace.

changed_touched.description: A name in an entry that the difference changes, in a permission set, a profile or a custom metadata record: a grant that is given, withdrawn or altered, or what a record binds. These are the "grants touched"; the reason for the row is the changed line. An entry is an element directly under the root of the file: one `<fieldPermissions>`, one `<classAccesses>`, one `<values>` of a record. A name is touched if its own line changed or if any line of its entry did, so that a change of `<readable>` touches the field that the entry names on a line of its own. Each version of the file is read on its own: `side` `head` rows are the names in the entries that have changed or added lines at head, and are `reference` rows of refs.jsonl; `side` `base` rows are the names in the entries that had changed or removed lines at base, read from the base version of the file and resolved against what the head declares. So a new grant has a row at head, a withdrawn one a row at base, and an altered one a row at each. What a custom metadata record is by its own name does not depend on a line: every change to the content of a record has a `cmdt_type` row for the type of the record, at each version the record has, and a `cmdt` row for whatever its own name names. The type is how code that queries the type as a whole is reached from a changed record. A file that only moved, with the same name in the same package directory, touches nothing. The file itself is a `symbol` row.

row.description: Input row discriminator, carried unchanged from changed.jsonl.

referrer.description: The `symbol` of the permission set, profile or custom metadata record that the file declares.

side.description: The version of the file the name was read from: `base` or `head`.

kind.description: As the `kind` of a refs.jsonl reference. `grant`: something a permission set or profile grants access to. `cmdt_field`: a field of its type that a record sets. `cmdt`: something a record names in a value or in its own name. `cmdt_type`: the custom metadata type of a record.

referenced.description: What is named: with `resolution` `declaration` the `symbol` of a declaration at head, otherwise the name as written.

referenced_type.description: What kind of thing `referenced` is, as the source says: the `referenced_type` of a refs.jsonl reference.

resolution.description: `declaration`: declared at head. `external`: in a namespace listed in the config file. `unresolved`: neither. A name read at base that the head no longer declares is `unresolved`, or `external`.

candidates.description: Present where the name may be one of several declarations that differ: the symbols of every one, sorted, each once. None is chosen.

package.description: The scope directory that `file` is under.

file.description: The permission set, profile or record file, relative to the root: its path at base for `side` `base`, at head for `head`.

line.description: Line of the name in that version of the file, counting from 1. A name that comes from the file's own name is at line 1.

changed_hunk.description: One hunk of the difference between the base and the head version of a file, without context: `@@ -base_start,base_lines +head_start,head_lines @@`, as in delta.jsonl, whose schema says how lines are compared. Nothing is ignored.

base_start.description: First line of the hunk at base, counting from 1. Where `base_lines` is 0 the hunk only adds lines, and this is the line at base that they come after: 0 for the top of the file.

base_lines.description: How many lines at base the hunk replaces or takes away.

head_start.description: First line of the hunk at head, counting from 1. Where `head_lines` is 0 the hunk only takes lines away, and this is the line at head that they came after: 0 for the top of the file. Such a hunk marks the innermost declaration at head that holds both that line and the next.

head_lines.description: How many lines at head the hunk changes or adds.

seed.description: Seed with direct referrers. Missing non-removed declarations are errors, not fabricated seeds.

symbol.description: API symbol with overload parameters. For an undeclared source, its referrer name or file path. Callable symbols preserve owner and member source spelling; parameter types are canonical: lowercase throughout, with System. removed from primitive and collection names, Iterable, Iterator, Object and SObject, and arrays written recursively as list<...>, without spaces. For example, Account.process(System.List<Id>) and Account.process(Id[]) both become Account.process(list<id>).

type.description: Declaration kind; file for a source without a declaration, unknown for an untyped touched name.

package.description: Normalised scope directory. Together with type and symbol this is the API identity.

file.description: Declaration file at head, or evidence file for an undeclared or removed seed. Distinguishes colliding declarations.

line.description: First declaration line, or evidence line for an undeclared touched name. Null when the input supplies no line.

scope.description: Scope provenance from extraction. Null for a node that refs do not declare: a removed symbol, a touched name or a file. Never inferred from directory spelling.

sources.description: All input evidence for this seed, sorted and deduplicated.

items.description: Original seed evidence; all changed symbol/touched rows retained, including base and head.

counts.description: Distinct direct reference rows per tier, independent of --depth. Expanded member/dispatch/binding/trigger links count each original row once. These are never transitive counts.

parsed.description: Number of direct parsed reference rows.

textual.description: Number of direct textual reference rows.

referrers.description: Direct incoming referrers grouped by source type. No transitive reference rows are repeated per seed.

test.description: Selected or possible @IsTest class. Apex does not allow a nested @IsTest class; where the source has one all the same, it is given as its top-level class, so that no dotted name, which no test run can be given, is emitted. Its own name stays in the witness path, in the seed where the path is empty, or in `convention`. Reasons are unioned across seeds; exactly one shortest witness is retained, with stable tie breaking. A convention or changed witness has an empty path.

symbol.description: API symbol with overload parameters. For an undeclared source, its referrer name or file path. Callable symbols preserve owner and member source spelling; parameter types are canonical: lowercase throughout, with System. removed from primitive and collection names, Iterable, Iterator, Object and SObject, and arrays written recursively as list<...>, without spaces. For example, Account.process(System.List<Id>) and Account.process(Id[]) both become Account.process(list<id>).

type.description: Declaration kind; file for a source without a declaration, unknown for an untyped touched name.

package.description: Normalised scope directory. Together with type and symbol this is the API identity.

file.description: Declaration file at head, or evidence file for an undeclared or removed seed. Distinguishes colliding declarations.

line.description: First declaration line, or evidence line for an undeclared touched name. Null when the input supplies no line.

scope.description: Scope provenance from extraction. Null for a node that refs do not declare: a removed symbol, a touched name or a file. Never inferred from directory spelling.

reasons.description: Distinct sorted reasons. A possible test is absent from tests.

items.description: Selection reason: changed selects the seed test; convention uses owner and suffixes; direct includes corroborated first-hop text; caller is a parsed path; trigger_dml bridges parsed DML; platform_entry follows parsed owner/constructor references for a method seed with no parsed referrer after dispatch/bindings. Only possible uses textual_path, lwc_textual and member_name_only (first-hop member text without same-file owner evidence).

convention.description: On a selected row with the reason convention: the inner @IsTest classes whose names matched a changed class and a suffix, where this row is their top-level class. They are kept apart from the one witness, which has an empty path for a convention match and may be of another seed or reason. Absent where the name that matched is this row's own.

seed.description: Seed responsible for this shortest witness.

path.description: One shortest witness across all seeds. Resolve its reference IDs through the shared table.

gap.description: One confidence limitation with its input location. Duplicate reason/location pairs are emitted once.

reason.description: Gap kind, including changed-file gaps, unresolved, ambiguous, scope_error, missing_declaration, trigger_entry or dynamic_binding. unverified_refs: the refs were of a tree that is `dirty` or `unknown`, which cannot be known to be the head that changed.jsonl was made for, and were used because `--accept-unverified-refs` was given: to sf-impact-tests (source refs), or to sf-impact-changed when it wrote changed.jsonl (source changed). What is selected may not be what the head would select. Refs that are known to be of another head are refused and give no document.

file.description: Input source file or missing scope directory. For unverified_refs, the input whose first row says so: `refs.jsonl` or `changed.jsonl`, by those names whatever the files are called, with line 1.

line.description: Source line if provided by the input, otherwise null; changed file rows have no lines.

identity.description: Compact declaration identity; full declarations appear on seeds and referrers.

symbol.description: API symbol including overload signature. Callable symbols preserve owner and member source spelling; parameter types are canonical: lowercase throughout, with System. removed from primitive and collection names, Iterable, Iterator, Object and SObject, and arrays written recursively as list<...>, without spaces. For example, Account.process(System.List<Id>) and Account.process(Id[]) both become Account.process(list<id>).

route.description: A target and expansion rule reached by at least one reference in this direct source/tier group. Original rows retain names and ambiguity candidates.

via.description: Why this edge reaches the seed: reference, seeded member, same-signature dispatch, targeted owner binding, trigger DML, or platform_entry (parsed owning-type/constructor reference when a method seed has no parsed incoming edge after dispatch and bindings). Expansions add no extra hop beyond the reference and never re-expand reached members.

evidence.description: Reference IDs proving dispatch inheritance or the trigger-to-object binding; empty for ordinary links.

items.description: Integer reference ID. Resolve with references[ID as a string]; IDs are sorted input row indices and need not be contiguous.

changed_provenance.description: What wrote the file, and of what: the first row of the file, and the only one of its kind. Before it maps anything, `sf-impact-changed` reads the first row of delta.jsonl and of refs.jsonl and holds the one to the other. The refs have to be of the head of the delta: `tree` says the commit that is the head, or a tree that is the tree of the head; and `root`, `scope` and `config` are the same in both. Each file has to be of a `schema` version that the tool knows. Anything else is refused in one line that names the field, what each file has for it, and what to run. A file without its first row is refused as of an older format. `sf-impact-tests` holds the refs.jsonl it is given to this row in the same way. Each tool first holds every row it reads to its schema, and refuses one that is not valid against it, so that no value that is not valid is carried from one file into the next. For this row that takes in what its fields say of each other: `base`, `head`, `head_tree`, `root`, `scope` and `config` are those of `inputs.delta`; `inputs.refs` are of that head, or of a tree that is no commit's; and `confidence` is `full` in the first case and `partial`, with its gap, in the second. The row holds no time, no name of a machine and no path of one, so the same two files still give a byte-identical file.

tool.description: The tool that wrote the file: `sf-impact-changed`.

version.description: The version of that tool, as its `--version` prints it. It says what wrote the file; what a tool reads is decided by `schema`.

schema.description: The version of this schema that the file is valid against: 1, the first to have this row. A tool refuses a file of a version it does not know. A file that does not start with this row is of the format before version 1 and is refused too.

base.description: The full id of the commit compared from, as the delta has it.

head.description: The full id of the commit compared to, as the delta has it. Refs that go with this file are of this commit.

head_tree.description: The id of the tree of the head, as the delta has it. Refs of another commit with this tree are refs of the head too.

root.description: Where the project is in the repository, as the delta has it. Refs that go with this file are of the same root.

scope.description: What the sfdx-project.json of the head declares: the same in the delta and in the refs.

config.description: The config of the head: the same in the delta and in the refs.

confidence.description: `full`: the refs were verified to be of the head of the delta. `partial`: they were not, for the reason in `gaps`, and were mapped all the same because the tool was told to. The confidence of the whole file is `partial` if any row says so, this one too.

gaps.description: Present where `confidence` is `partial`, and only there. `unverified_refs`: the refs were of a tree that is `dirty` or `unknown` (see `inputs`), which cannot be known to be the head, and `--accept-unverified-refs` was given. The declarations and lines that the difference was mapped onto may not be those of the head. `sf-impact-tests` gives this as a reason for the partial confidence of what it writes.

inputs.description: The first rows of the two files that were read, as they are, each without its `row`. Each is valid by the schema of its file.

refs_provenance.description: The first row of the refs.jsonl that was read, without its `row`: refs.schema.json says what each field is.

delta_provenance.description: The first row of the delta.jsonl that was read, without its `row`: delta.schema.json says what each field is. Its `scope` and `config` are never null here: a delta whose head has no project file or no config that can be read is refused.

provenance_tree.description: The tree that was read, as far as it is known. Before it reads a file, `sf-impact-extract` asks git which commit is checked out where `--root` is and what that commit holds (`rev-parse`, `ls-tree`): plumbing that reads and writes nothing, run without any `GIT_*` variable of the caller's and without the user's and the system's configuration, as `sf-impact-delta` runs it. It asks git nothing after. What it reads is sfdx-project.json, sf-impact.json if there is one, and every file under the scope directories, each once, and of the bytes that it read of each it works out the id that git gives such content, itself. Those ids and the set of files are held to the commit. So the comparison is of the very bytes that the rows are made of, and a file that changes while the tool runs is the commit's only if what was read of it is. Nothing else counts: a file outside the scope is not read, whatever git says of it, and a file in scope that the commit does not have counts though git ignores it. A file's mode is not content. Refs are of the head of a delta if `commit` is its head or `tree` is the tree of its head, and `root` is its `root`.

oneOf.description: Every file that was read is as this commit has it, and the commit has no file in scope that was not read: the tree is a clean checkout of the commit, as far as it was read.

commit.description: The full id of the commit that is checked out.

tree.description: The id of the tree of that commit. Another commit with the same tree has the same content: the commit rebased, amended or squashed without a change. Refs of this commit are refs of that one. One commit has one tree: refs that name the head of a delta and another tree than it has are refused.

oneOf.description: `dirty`: the root is in a repository with a commit checked out, and what was read is not what that commit has: a file in scope is changed, new, ignored or gone, or the commit has a directory in scope that is not on disk. `sf-impact-extract` says which file on standard error. `unknown`: no commit could be read: the root is in no repository, the repository has no commit, there is no git, or git refuses the repository because another user owns it (`--trust-repo` has it read). Neither can be verified to be of any commit. `sf-impact-changed` and `sf-impact-tests` refuse such refs with a delta, unless they are told to use them as they are (`--accept-unverified-refs`), and then say in their output that they did.

provenance_id.description: The id of a git object, in full: 40 hexadecimal digits, or 64 in a repository that uses SHA-256.

provenance_root.description: Where the project is in its repository: the path of the directory that holds sfdx-project.json, from the top of the repository, with `/` between its parts and without `.` segments or a trailing separator; `.` where the project is at the top. Never a path of the machine. One commit can hold several projects, each declaring the same directories: this is what tells the refs of one from the refs of another.

provenance_scope.description: The scope directories that sfdx-project.json declares, as paths from the root with `/` separators and without `.` segments or a trailing separator, as every `package` is written. Each list is sorted by the bytes of the paths and has each path once. A declared path that leaves the root, absolute or with `..`, holds nothing in scope and is in neither list. A directory that both keys name is in `packageDirectories` alone. A declared directory that is not on disk is still declared, and is listed. An empty scope path denotes the project root.

unpackagedMetadata.description: The `unpackagedMetadata.path` of every entry of `packageDirectories` that has one.

provenance_config.description: A hash of the config as it takes effect, not of the file sf-impact.json as it is written: 16 hexadecimal digits in lower case, the FNV-1a hash of 64 bits of the UTF-8 text `{"namespaces":[..],"textualAllowList":[..],"textualMinLength":n}`, written without white space, each list with its names in ASCII lower case, sorted by their bytes, each once. So a tree with no config file, one with `{}` and one that states the defaults all hash as `4e7844462778448c`, and keys that are for other tools change nothing. It tells two configs apart. It is no protection against a file made to deceive, and neither is the rest of the row.
